events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.43 (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra kilometres on an unexempted off-route segment flow straight into the fare under RD-1 and RD-2; the trip drove 18.7 km against a 13.9 km optimal route and billed $6.77 of excess distance [F1][F4][F16-RD-2]. The only measured deviation is one off-route segment, 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km (+4.56 km) [F3].

RD-4 does not excuse it: the trace shows no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch, and the only traffic facts are central-expressway and Kampong Bahru Road speed band 5 (40–49 km/h), which on their own do not exempt a segment [F12][F13][F14][RD-4(a)][RD-4(b)].

RD-5 / RD-3 turn on what the chat actually says. The driver asked "Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty." [F8] and the rider replied "Sure, no problem." [F9] — that is agreement to a stop the driver proposed, not a route authorisation. The rider never chose the place: the driver named the station and named its location ("just ahead"), so this is not RD-3(a) — the rider did not name a place, and the record still shows no measured stop [F8][F9][F3][RD-3(a)]. The driver's own statement confirms the scope was a short stop and that he extended it himself into "a small change of route" [F11]; a scope-creep justification in a post-trip statement is a claim, not rider consent [RD-5][G11]. Under RD-5 the agreement covers a short stop, not a 6.27 km loop; no rider message before 21:39:55 authorises the route driven, so the segment counts and the extra km are refundable under RD-2 [F3][F5-F6][RD-5][RD-2].

Amount: rate = $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.40997.../km (as the fare record states); 4.56 km × $1.40997/km = $6.4295 → $6.43 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The waiting charge $0.11 for 0.4 min is a metered waiting unit and is not refundable [F5][RD-3(c)]. The $1.25/$1.47 platform fee is a published fee [F7][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not attach: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no flag_account [F17][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.43 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment (RD-2, paid as voucher per NS-7); record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file — no account flag as the RD-6 threshold is not met.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We've reviewed your trip and are giving you a $6.43 Ryde voucher.

Your driver took a 6.27 km detour between 21:39 and 21:49, while the direct route for that stretch is only 1.71 km — an extra 4.56 km added to your metered fare. Nothing in the trip record shows a road incident that would have justified going that way.

What the driver asked you about was stopping briefly at a petrol station, and you agreed to that. That agreement didn't cover the longer route that was actually driven, so the extra distance is refunded.

The voucher is added to your Ryde account. Your driver's file has been noted; your own account is unaffected.

DRIVER: We've reviewed the trip dispute on this fare and upheld it in part.

Your meter ran 18.7 km against a 13.9 km best route. The only unexcused stretch is one off-route segment between 21:39 and 21:49 — 6.27 km driven where the direct route covers 1.71 km. No qualifying traffic incident appears on that stretch, and the rider's agreement to your short petrol stop did not extend to the route you took.

Result: a $6.43 Ryde voucher is issued to the rider for the extra distance. No account flag is added, as your recent record doesn't reach the threshold.

This breach stays on your file. Keep to the metered best route unless the rider agrees to a change.
